content.text:
Start at https://www.linkedin.com and complete the following task.

I’m trying to figure out whether I should focus my post-grad job search on New York City for film and adjacent media work, and I want a real browser-based sweep instead of just a few random listings. Start with LinkedIn, but don’t stay stuck there if better public pages exist. I want you to find exactly 18 current NYC-area opportunities that are genuinely entry-level, internship, assistant, coordinator, production, post-production, development, distribution, exhibition, or other clearly film-related early-career roles. Use a mix of public sources such as LinkedIn job pages, company careers pages, entertainment job boards, and studio or production-company hiring pages, and make sure at least 6 of the 18 come from sources other than LinkedIn so this is not just one-site sampling. For each opportunity, record the title, company, borough or city area if shown, whether it is internship or full-time, whether it looks remote, hybrid, or on-site, salary or pay if shown, and the key qualifications or software/tools mentioned; if any field is missing, mark it as not shown. As you work, open and keep visible the strongest evidence tabs for at least 8 of the listings, including a mix of source types and at least 3 actual employer career pages, so I can sanity-check that the openings are real. After collecting the 18 roles, compare them and identify the 6 best fits for a recent graduate with limited professional experience but serious interest in film, and briefly explain why those 6 rise to the top based on accessibility, relevance, and transparency of requirements. Then give me a short synthesis of what this search suggests about the NYC entry-level film market right now: which role types appear most often, whether paid opportunities seem common enough, and whether the market looks broad enough that I should concentrate my search there for the next few weeks. Leave the final shortlist and the most useful evidence tabs open. Make a spreadsheet with all the listings and the links to apply.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

  return arr.map(val => {
    const s = String(val ?? "");
    if (s.includes(",") || s.includes('"') || s.includes("\n")) {
      return `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
    }
    return s;
  }).join(",");
}

const headers = ["Title", "Company", "Borough / City Area", "Role Type", "Work Mode", "Salary / Pay", "Key Qualifications & Software / Tools", "Source Type", "Application Link"];
const csvLines = [toCSVLine(headers)];

for (const row of listings) {
  csvLines.push(toCSVLine([
    row.title,
    row.company,
    row.borough_area,
    row.role_type,
    row.work_mode,
    row.salary_pay,
    row.qualifications_tools,
    row.source_type,
    row.link
  ]));
}

const csvContent = csvLines.join("\n");

// Write to downloadable file in REPL
writeFile("nyc_film_entry_level_opportunities.csv", csvContent, "text/csv");

// Also save artifact
const artifactResult = await tool.artifact({
  action: "write",
  path: "files/",
  filename: "nyc_film_entry_level_opportunities.csv",
  content: csvContent,
  mime_type: "text/csv"
});

console.log("CSV created and saved successfully! Artifact:", artifactResult);
console.log(`Total listings in CSV: ${listings.length}`);

- **Source Type**: LinkedIn Job Page
- **Application Link**: https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/video-producer-fellowship-at-semafor-4454850909

---

### Top 6 Best Fits for a Recent Graduate

For a recent graduate with limited professional experience but serious film interest, the 6 best opportunities stand out based on **accessibility** (realistic entry barriers without requiring multi-year industry tenure), **relevance** (substantive film industry learning and networking), and **transparency** (explicit pay, defined duties, and clear growth trajectories):

1. **NewForm — Production Assistant ($48K–$58K/yr, NYC)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: This is one of the purest entry-level production roles in the city. The employer explicitly states that gear familiarity and prior student film/freelance experience are "a plus, not required" and guarantees a formal promotional track toward Associate Producer. It gives immediate on-set repetitions leading simple shoots and assisting on larger setups.

2. **AbelCine — Rental Prep Technician ($45K–$50K/yr, Brooklyn Industry City)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Rental houses are the premier training ground for film graduates who want technical mastery. AbelCine is the epicenter of NYC cinema gear rentals. Prepping and checking out ARRI, RED, Sony, and Canon camera packages puts a new grad in direct daily contact with NYC Directors of Photography, camera operators, and ACs, building high-value industry relationships that accelerate a camera/lighting career.

3. **Sony Pictures (Sony Pictures Classics) — Exhibitor Relations Coordinator ($27.20/hr, ~$56.5K/yr, Manhattan)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Sony Pictures Classics is headquartered in Manhattan and is the preeminent theatrical distributor of independent and prestige arthouse cinema. The role does not require senior corporate experience (bachelor's preferred, passion for theatrical film required) and places the candidate right at the nexus of film distribution, trailer tracking, and direct relationship-building with Manhattan theater managers.

4. **WME — Rotational Assistant ($21.00/hr, ~$43.7K/yr, Manhattan 11 Madison)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: The agency mailroom/floater pool remains the classic Hollywood and NYC gateway for aspiring development executives, agents, and producers. The role specifically trains assistants on script reading and script coverage (evaluating screenplays for agents), providing immediate exposure to how deals are packaged and projects get financed.

5. **Nicolosi & Co., Inc. — Agency Assistant ($45K–$50K/yr, Manhattan Boutique Agency)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Unlike sprawling corporate talent agencies where assistants are siloed into back-office tasks, this boutique agency supports actors across NYC film, television, and Broadway. The posting explicitly notes that previous entertainment agency experience is "a plus" (not a prerequisite), offers a hybrid schedule with remote Fridays, and uses core industry platforms (Breakdown Express, Vimeo, InEntertainment).

6. **Rooftop Films — Assistant Venue Manager ($20.00/hr, Outdoor NYC Screenings)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Rooftop Films is the heartbeat of NYC's independent and community film exhibition scene. Entry requirements are accessible (hospitality or event interest, with fireguard certification reimbursed), and it embeds the candidate in front-of-house operations, 35mm/digital projection workflows, and networking with visiting indie filmmakers across all five boroughs.

---

### Synthesis of the NYC Entry-Level Film & Media Market

1. **Which role types appear most often?**
   - **Post-Production & Technical Asset Logistics**: Post-production finishing houses (Company 3, Resillion) and studio media operations (Paramount, Amazon MGM+, WITHIN) represent the highest volume of structured entry-level postings. Titles like Media Coordinator, Color Assist, and Mastering QC Operator are in consistent demand due to streaming delivery requirements.
   - **Rental & Camera Prep**: NYC’s vibrant camera rental ecosystem (AbelCine in Industry City, Adorama Rental Company) consistently hires technicians to maintain and inspect cinema packages.
   - **Talent Representation & Agency Desks**: The major agencies (WME, CAA) and boutique shops (Nicolosi & Co.) regularly cycle through rotational assistants and agency floater pools.
   - **Festival & Exhibition Operations**: Spring and summer bring seasonal spikes from organizations like Tribeca Festival and Rooftop Films for programming and venue management.

2. **Are paid opportunities common enough?**
   - **Yes, and pay transparency is exceptionally high**: Thanks to NYC’s Pay Transparency Law, nearly every legitimate corporate and boutique listing publishes an exact hourly or annual compensation figure. Entry-level hourly wages generally fall between **$20.00 and $29.00 per hour** ($41,600 to $60,300 annualized), while full-time entry salaries range from **$45,000 to $65,000 per year**. Unpaid internships still exist at small non-profits, but the mainstream entry-level market in NYC is thoroughly paid.

3. **Is the market broad enough to concentrate your search here for the next few weeks?**
   - **Yes, with a specific strategic focus**: If your interest is in independent film, documentary, theatrical distribution, post-production finishing, or agency representation, NYC is one of the two best markets in North America (rivaled only by Los Angeles). Unlike LA, which leans heavily toward studio development and large-scale studio lots, NYC has a denser concentration of independent distributors (A24, Sony Pictures Classics, IFC Films, Kino Lorber), camera rental hubs in Brooklyn, and prestige exhibition institutions. Concentrating your search in NYC over the next several weeks is well justified, especially if you target rental houses, post-production finishing studios, and agency desks alongside traditional production companies.

ABOUT THE ROLE
Tribeca is seeking a Seasonal Shorts Programmer to join the Programming team for the 2027 Tribeca Festival. Reporting to the VP, Shorts Programming, this role will play an active part in reviewing and evaluating short film submissions, developing and curating shorts programs, identifying emerging filmmakers and storytellers, and helping shape a compelling shorts lineup for the Festival.
The Shorts Programmer will bring a strong knowledge of the short film landscape, a thoughtful curatorial perspective, and an understanding of what creates both audience excitement and industry interest. The role will work collaboratively with the Shorts Programming team throughout the selection and programming process and will participate in Festival events and activities related to the shorts program.
This is a seasonal position from September - June and requires regular film screening and evaluation, participation in weekly programming meetings, and on-site involvement during the 2027 Tribeca Festival.
ABOUT YOU
The ideal candidate has deep knowledge of the short film landscape and experience programming or evaluating short films, preferably within a film festival environment. You are excited by the opportunity to discover new films and storytellers and understand the responsibility involved in evaluating a large submission pool and helping shape it into a highly selective Festival program.
You bring creativity and imagination to curation and enjoy exploring how individual films can be brought together around themes, ideas, and perspectives to create thought-provoking and memorable audience experiences. You are equally comfortable working independently and collaborating with a broader programming team.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Review, evaluate, and recommend short film submissions for consideration for the 2027 Tribeca Festival.
Contribute to the curation of short film programs, including identifying programming themes and recommending ways films can be paired to create compelling audience experiences.
Participate actively in Shorts Programming meetings and discussions throughout the review, selection, and programming process.

Venue Manager (Seasonal)

Rooftop Films is looking for part-time Venue Managers to take a crucial role in the production and operations of our 30th anniversary Summer Series film festival, taking place May through September 2026 at outdoor locations throughout NYC. This is a flexible, creative position, employing a variety of skills. The Venue Manager will assist with on-site management of Rooftop Films Summer Series screenings. We are looking for candidates who have availability for part-time work from May through early September, averaging 20-30 hours per week.

Responsibilities include light pre-season preparations (including orientation and site visits), liaison to sponsors, execution of sponsorship activations, as well as supporting the Festival Producer and Operations Coordinator in general event preparation and execution as needed. Rooftop Films screens in multiple locations that require unique event management systems and procedures; since there are many venues, each with their own particulars, certain basics change from venue to venue. This position reports directly to the Festival Producer and Operations Coordinator.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

On-Site Event Management
Act as primary liaison between Rooftop Films staff and venue staff to ensure clear communication and that all venue procedures are adhered to. 
Oversee internal and external security staff in audience safety procedures (per city and state guidelines)
Coordinate with venue staff and Box Office Coordinator to create a plan for audience traffic flow and procedures
Coordinate with venue staff and tech crew to communicate needs about safety and strike
Manage and lead event support staff: 
Arrive on site early to help organize and lead the unload and set up of the FOH supplies with the FOH team
Work with Box Office Coordinator to ensure smooth check in and audience load in procedures
Supervise set-up of any necessary tables, tents, or other supplies/staging needed for Rooftop Films staff, vendors, and sponsors
Oversee crowd flow, ushering, security, audience relations, permit compliance, and safety protocols, including weather preparedness for speedy strikes or working in sustained heat
Work with the Volunteer Coordinator to ensure volunteers have suitable roles and assistance (where appropriate) from the FOH team and Box Office. 
Develop an on-site strike plan with tech crew and Volunteer Coordinator to ensure everything is properly loaded and nothing is left behind 
Execute the FOH Run of Show 
Send show notes and show reports to Festival Producer and Operations Coordinator before leaving venue 
Communicate clearly and consistently with office staff, on-site crew, and tech to ensure smooth Run of Show, including meetings on site as needed to coordinate last minute changes
Event Planning
In collaboration with the Festival Producer and Operations Coordinator, and other office FOH staff

We are seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented, and motivated Agency Assistant to support 2 of our 4 agents with the day-to-day operations of a busy talent agency representing actors across film, television, and theatre.

A college degree is required. The ideal candidate is a proactive team player with excellent communication skills. Prior experience in an entertainment agency, talent management, casting, or a related field is a plus, as is familiarity with Breakdown Express, Vimeo, InEntertainment, and Canva. Hungry for information, they read the trades regularly.

Key responsibilities include but are not limited to assisting agents with daily office operations, managing audition appointments, updating client records and materials, coordinating calendars and meetings, and tracking air dates, openings, showcases, and bookings.

Other responsibilities include administrative tasks such as monitoring office emails, answering phones/checking voicemails, and welcoming office guests.

Hours are 9:45 - 6:00 PM. This is an in-office position. We work remotely on Fridays only.

Salary/Benefits
$45,000.00 - 50,000.00 per year


Additional Information
Passion, business acumen, taste: These are just some of the hallmarks of this established boutique agency.
Having represented clients in the framework of traditional agencies, Jeanne Nicolosi recognized the emerging changes in entertainment media and live performance markets and felt that a more open, flexible, nimble, and team-oriented form of representation could offer greater opportunities for talent.
In 2002 she established nicolosi & co. which quickly became one of New York's most respected agencies in the areas of film, television and theatre.

nicolosi & co.'s finely culled client list, experienced team of associates, and hands on managerial style make this agency a sought after destination for actors seeking finely customized representation ''without borders.''

In short, they offer Exclusive representation for exclusive actors.

// Helper to escape CSV values
function toCSVLine(arr) {
  return arr.map(val => {
    const s = String(val ?? "");
    if (s.includes(",") || s.includes('"') || s.includes("\n")) {
      return `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
    }
    return s;
  }).join(",");
}

const headers = ["Title", "Company", "Borough / City Area", "Role Type", "Work Mode", "Salary / Pay", "Key Qualifications & Software / Tools", "Source Type", "Application Link"];
const csvLines = [toCSVLine(headers)];

    row.borough_area,
    row.role_type,
    row.work_mode,
    row.salary_pay,
    row.qualifications_tools,
    row.source_type,
    row.link
  ]));
}

const csvContent = csvLines.join("\n");

// Write to downloadable file in REPL
writeFile("nyc_film_entry_level_opportunities.csv", csvContent, "text/csv");

// Also save artifact
const artifactResult = await tool.artifact({
  action: "write",
  path: "files/",
  filename: "nyc_film_entry_level_opportunities.csv",
  content: csvContent,
  mime_type: "text/csv"
});

// Helper to escape CSV values
function toCSVLine(arr) {
  return arr.map(val => {
    const s = String(val ?? "");
    if (s.includes(",") || s.includes('"') || s.includes("\n")) {
      return `"${s.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
    }
    return s;
  }).join(",");
}

const headers = ["Title", "Company", "Borough / City Area", "Role Type", "Work Mode", "Salary / Pay", "Key Qualifications & Software / Tools", "Source Type", "Application Link"];
const csvLines = [toCSVLine(headers)];

for (const row of listings) {
  csvLines.push(toCSVLine([
    row.title,
    row.company,
    row.borough_area,
    row.role_type,
    row.work_mode,
    row.salary_pay,
    row.qualifications_tools,
    row.source_type,
    row.link
  ]));
}

const csvContent = csvLines.join("\n");

// Write to downloadable file in REPL
writeFile("nyc_film_entry_level_opportunities.csv", csvContent, "text/csv");

// Also save artifact
const artifactResult = await tool.artifact({
  action: "write",
  path: "files/",
  filename: "nyc_film_entry_level_opportunities.csv",
  content: csvContent,
  mime_type: "text/csv"
});

console.log("CSV created and saved successfully! Artifact:", artifactResult);
console.log(`Total listings in CSV: ${listings.length}`);
"}

### Top 6 Best Fits for a Recent Graduate

For a recent graduate with limited professional experience but serious film interest, the 6 best opportunities stand out based on **accessibility** (realistic entry barriers without requiring multi-year industry tenure), **relevance** (substantive film industry learning and networking), and **transparency** (explicit pay, defined duties, and clear growth trajectories):

1. **NewForm — Production Assistant ($48K–$58K/yr, NYC)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: This is one of the purest entry-level production roles in the city. The employer explicitly states that gear familiarity and prior student film/freelance experience are "a plus, not required" and guarantees a formal promotional track toward Associate Producer. It gives immediate on-set repetitions leading simple shoots and assisting on larger setups.

2. **AbelCine — Rental Prep Technician ($45K–$50K/yr, Brooklyn Industry City)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Rental houses are the premier training ground for film graduates who want technical mastery. AbelCine is the epicenter of NYC cinema gear rentals. Prepping and checking out ARRI, RED, Sony, and Canon camera packages puts a new grad in direct daily contact with NYC Directors of Photography, camera operators, and ACs, building high-value industry relationships that accelerate a camera/lighting career.

3. **Sony Pictures (Sony Pictures Classics) — Exhibitor Relations Coordinator ($27.20/hr, ~$56.5K/yr, Manhattan)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Sony Pictures Classics is headquartered in Manhattan and is the preeminent theatrical distributor of independent and prestige arthouse cinema. The role does not require senior corporate experience (bachelor's preferred, passion for theatrical film required) and places the candidate right at the nexus of film distribution, trailer tracking, and direct relationship-building with Manhattan theater managers.

4. **WME — Rotational Assistant ($21.00/hr, ~$43.7K/yr, Manhattan 11 Madison)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: The agency mailroom/floater pool remains the classic Hollywood and NYC gateway for aspiring development executives, agents, and producers. The role specifically trains assistants on script reading and script coverage (evaluating screenplays for agents), providing immediate exposure to how deals are packaged and projects get financed.

5. **Nicolosi & Co., Inc. — Agency Assistant ($45K–$50K/yr, Manhattan Boutique Agency)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Unlike sprawling corporate talent agencies where assistants are siloed into back-office tasks, this boutique agency supports actors across NYC film, television, and Broadway. The posting explicitly notes that previous entertainment agency experience is "a plus" (not a prerequisite), offers a hybrid schedule with remote Fridays, and uses core industry platforms (Breakdown Express, Vimeo, InEntertainment).

6. **Rooftop Films — Assistant Venue Manager ($20.00/hr, Outdoor NYC Screenings)**
   - *Why it rises to the top*: Rooftop Films is the heartbeat of NYC's independent and community film exhibition scene. Entry requirements are accessible (hospitality or event interest, with fireguard certification reimbursed), and it embeds the candidate in front-of-house operations, 35mm/digital projection workflows, and networking with visiting indie filmmakers across all five boroughs.

### Synthesis of the NYC Entry-Level Film & Media Market

1. **Which role types appear most often?**
   - **Post-Production & Technical Asset Logistics**: Post-production finishing houses (Company 3, Resillion) and studio media operations (Paramount, Amazon MGM+, WITHIN) represent the highest volume of structured entry-level postings. Titles like Media Coordinator, Color Assist, and Mastering QC Operator are in consistent demand due to streaming delivery requirements.
   - **Rental & Camera Prep**: NYC’s vibrant camera rental ecosystem (AbelCine in Industry City, Adorama Rental Company) consistently hires technicians to maintain and inspect cinema packages.
   - **Talent Representation & Agency Desks**: The major agencies (WME, CAA) and boutique shops (Nicolosi & Co.) regularly cycle through rotational assistants and agency floater pools.
   - **Festival & Exhibition Operations**: Spring and summer bring seasonal spikes from organizations like Tribeca Festival and Rooftop Films for programming and venue management.

2. **Are paid opportunities common enough?**
   - **Yes, and pay transparency is exceptionally high**: Thanks to NYC’s Pay Transparency Law, nearly every legitimate corporate and boutique listing publishes an exact hourly or annual compensation figure. Entry-level hourly wages generally fall between **$20.00 and $29.00 per hour** ($41,600 to $60,300 annualized), while full-time entry salaries range from **$45,000 to $65,000 per year**. Unpaid internships still exist at small non-profits, but the mainstream entry-level market in NYC is thoroughly paid.

3. **Is the market broad enough to concentrate your search here for the next few weeks?**
   - **Yes, with a specific strategic focus**: If your interest is in independent film, documentary, theatrical distribution, post-production finishing, or agency representation, NYC is one of the two best markets in North America (rivaled only by Los Angeles). Unlike LA, which leans heavily toward studio development and large-scale studio lots, NYC has a denser concentration of independent distributors (A24, Sony Pictures Classics, IFC Films, Kino Lorber), camera rental hubs in Brooklyn, and prestige exhibition institutions. Concentrating your search in NYC over the next several weeks is well justified, especially if you target rental houses, post-production finishing studios, and agency desks alongside traditional production companies.
